mode: concise fact extraction + consolidation by deepseek-flash (thinking disabled), embeddings bge-m3 from the shared endpoint, the server's default local reranker, observation recall as the plugin's default
how: retain: POST /memories {content, timestamp, document_id} per memory; ranked: POST /memories/recall (budget mid, max_tokens 4096), first 10; deployed: POST /memories/recall with the plugin's body (budget low, max_tokens 2000, include.entities null, types ["observation"])
notes: System under test: the Hindsight server (hindsight-api-slim 1.2.1, source at git 5318be8) with its default retrieval: four arms (semantic, keyword, graph, temporal) fused, then the server's local cross-encoder reranker. The DSH plugin is a client of this server; its per-session default injects a model-written reflect answer at the first prompt, which is not a list of memories and is not measured. Its retrieval-only option (autoInject recall) is what deployed follows.

Write path: the product extracts facts with a model (concise mode) and consolidates them into observations. hindsight-chunks bypasses that: each memory is stored as one verbatim chunk (document_id = the memory id, timestamp = its date at 12:00 UTC) and consolidation is off, which the server needs when no model is configured. Facts, entities and observations are therefore not measured in that configuration.
Embeddings: the server's default is a local English model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5); the shared bge-m3 endpoint is used instead (the benchmark's Chinese data); the reranker stays the server's default.

ids come from the document_id of each result (each memory is its own document). In the LLM configurations an observation has no document_id: it is given the id of the earliest memory (by date) among the documents of its source facts, which the recall returns when asked (include.source_facts); the deployed list is read from that call, an untimed repeat of the plugin-body call (ms times the plugin body without source facts), and llm_usage.observation_id_mapping counts the mapped observations and the repeats whose list differed. The API returns results in rank order without scores: scores are rank-derived. A memory appears once per list.
deployed budget: the plugin's recall body (budget low, max_tokens 2000). The recall clock is the real clock (the plugin passes no query timestamp), about a month after the last memory.
ms is the wall-clock time of one deployed recall call over HTTP on localhost, including the server's reranker.

Which configuration stands for what: hindsight-llm-<model> is the system as its server works by default (a model extracts facts from each memory and consolidates them into observations; the model is the only setting changed, with thinking disabled); hindsight-chunks is its mode without a model (each memory stored verbatim as one chunk, no extraction, no consolidation). The plugin's own default injection (a model-written reflect answer at the first prompt) is not a list of memories and is not measured in any configuration.

Paid configurations: the server's model calls pass through llm_proxy.py (127.0.0.1 inside the container), which forwards each request and its answer unchanged except for the thinking switch ({"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}, also set through HINDSIGHT_API_LLM_EXTRA_BODY) and the removal of temperature/top_p/top_k for claude-haiku-5-5 (the server sends none); tokens, cached tokens, reasoning tokens, status codes, rate-limit responses and retries are counted from the provider's own answers (see llm_usage). The server's startup connection check is one counted call.
